questions.text: What does the bottom line of an income statement represent?
options: Profit after expenses, taxes, and salaries
Amount of cash generated from operations
questions.explanation: The bottom line shows the profit remaining after all expenses, taxes, and salaries are subtracted from revenue.

questions.text: What does the cash flow statement primarily track?
options: Physical cash moving in and out from operations, investing, and financing activities
Total revenue earned over a fiscal year
The company's market share relative to competitors
The proportion of debt to equity in the capital structure
questions.explanation: It records the actual cash inflows and outflows from the three main business activities.

questions.text: True or false: A durable competitive advantage, such as brand strength or high switching costs, helps protect a company's profit margins over time.
questions.explanation: A strong moat protects profit margins year after year even when the economy faces headwinds.

questions.text: True or false: The debt-to-equity ratio measures how effectively management uses owners' money to generate profits.
questions.explanation: Debt-to-equity assesses financial leverage, whereas return on equity evaluates profit generation from equity.
